findings.evidence: **Trap.** `outline: none` with no replacement: keyboard users lose their place (SC 2.4.7). A control that looks disabled and still submits.
findings.fix: Shorten these activation-level traps to the bare reminder (`outline: none` without a `:focus-visible` replacement fails). Use the saved lines for a non-obvious fact, for example a MUI `disableRipple` or `focusVisibleClassName` override that removes the visible ring.

findings.evidence: 4. Review or verdict: pick the row of Input that matches what you have, then emit the table under Review output.
findings.fix: Add a short evidence-gathering sequence for reviews: (1) open the stylesheets and shared components the target imports, (2) find the theme so a `var()` or theme reference can be resolved before tokens and a11y are decided, (3) trace every request to its branches before states and loading are decided, then fill the table.

findings.evidence: ## NEVER — three items: no second theme, no invented line numbers, no UNVERIFIED figure as a fail line
findings.fix: Add: 'NEVER pass a11y contrast for a color read through a theme reference you have not resolved: the token name passes tokens, but its value can still sit under 3:1 in the dark theme.'

findings.evidence: 26 queries: 15 should-trigger and 11 should-not-trigger. Five of the positives are bare phrases ('review this page', 'make this look polished before the demo') that repeat the description's own trigger wording.
findings.fix: Bring the set to about 10 positives and 10 negatives. Replace the phrases taken from the description with indirect, context-heavy positives (file paths, a component name, a symptom) so the file tests whether the description generalises.

findings.evidence: Exactly this header, then eight rows in this order ... One defect, one row — but nothing says how to report several defects of the same rule, or several files or views, in one row
findings.fix: Add under Review output: 'When a rule has several defects, put each file:line in the one evidence cell, separated by `; `, and one imperative fix per defect in the same order in the fix cell. With several files or views, prefix each piece of evidence with its file.'
